$comment: The M1 crafting chain, per design-bible §5. Every recipe runs as a time-gated industry job (§6). Job durations and level gates are first-draft numbers expected to move once EconSim can measure the economy — which is exactly why they live here rather than in code.

recipes.$comment: The first craft. Deliberately needs no tool, or the chain could never start. No mainInput: scrap is common to every world, so the laser is Common whoever makes it (Joe, 10 October 2026, task 187).

Terra's. One of four recipes for the same plate, one per homeworld's ore (ADR-0008: a crafted good is one item made by per-race recipes that consume different raw inputs; task 185). Identical numbers on all four, so no race refines faster or cheaper than another, and TheOpeningCanBeWalkedTests walks the questline from each world with only that world's ore. The key keeps the old name because industry jobs refer to it.
Ares'. The same plate from oxide salt; see refine_ferrite_plate.
Verdance's. The same plate from rootstone; see refine_ferrite_plate.
Grimhold's. The same plate from blackiron ore; see refine_ferrite_plate.

Level 1 for the same reason build_shuttle_hull_section is: it is the only source of electronics XP in the pack, so anything above 1 is a skill nobody can start. The inputs are the two materials a player already has by this point in the questline -- no third gathering loop to introduce one component -- and it is deliberately cheaper than the hull section it is fitted to, because a thruster is the smaller half of a shuttle.

Level 1, and it has to be. Every source of shipcrafting XP in the pack is a recipe requiring level 5 or more, or a quest rewarded for running one of them -- so a requirement above 1 here is a skill nobody can ever start, and the onboarding chain stopped dead at 'Bones of a Ship' (task 148). The same reasoning craft_crude_mining_laser records for needing no tool: or the chain could never start.

The first recipe no race can satisfy alone. Two of its four raw inputs are always on the far side of the faction line, so building one means either trading at the capital's global market or hauling through contested space -- which is what makes the war economic rather than decorative (ADR-0008). Everything before it stays self-sufficient within a race on purpose, so a new player never stalls waiting for a market that may be empty. No mainInput: four worlds' materials with none in charge, so the frame is Common, and so is the freighter built from it (task 187). Task 178's fusion style for high tiers would replace that.

What a composite frame is for. build_alloy_frame had no consumer at all, so the frame -- the one item forcing material across the faction line -- had no standing demand, and EconSim showed cross-faction trade dying inside the first months of a five-year run. Two frames rather than one so the demand is worth a builder's while, and it reuses shuttle sections and thrusters rather than inventing new inputs, so the tier above the shuttle is reachable with skills the player already has. Level 25 leaves shipcrafting somewhere to go past the shuttle's 10 and the frame's 20.

Task 194: the tier-1 Laser Rifle, from what a player has by the end of the opening -- plate and scrap -- so the first weapon needs no new gathering loop. Level 1, as every first recipe of a skill must be, or nobody can start it (task 148). Its look is its plate's world's, as a thruster's is (task 187). First numbers.
